da-false-claim.evidence: hadron-operations-closure.md:16 states the skein relation as $q\cdot L_+ - q^{-1}\cdot L_- = (q-q^{-1})L_0$.
da-false-claim.notes: AGENTS.md §7a fixes the canonical skein relation as $\sigma_i-\sigma_i^{-1}=q-q^{-1}$, i.e. $L_+-L_-=(q-q^{-1})L_0$ (unweighted). The block's q-weighted variant $qL_+-q^{-1}L_-$ is a non-standard normalization; not strictly false (it is a valid rescaling if the eigenvalues are $(q,-q^{-1})$) but it deviates from the repo's STRICT Hecke-Skein convention and should cite which normalization is in play. Item 1 'antisymmetric product gives $-1$ on exchanging identical constituents' is correct for fermionic Sym.

da-vacuous.evidence: hadron-operations-closure.lean:35-48 — theorem hadron_operations_closure proves only $\forall h, \exists h', h'=\mathrm{op}(h)$, discharged by `⟨_, rfl⟩`.
da-vacuous.notes: The Lean statement is content-free: $\exists h'.\,h'=f(h)$ is trivially true for ANY total function f (witness = f(h)). It asserts nothing about braiding being an involution, Hopf linking being invertible, skein resolving to a q-polynomial, or fusion respecting structure — all the actual mathematical content of the .md proposition. This is the self-witnessing-existential anti-pattern.

da-overclaim.evidence: hadron-operations-closure.md:6-8 claims 'braiding descends to an involution'; .md:19 claims skein 'resolves any linked composite ... yielding the mass formula $\mathcal{M}(\mathfrak{H})=Q(q)\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{Hopf})+\sum_i\mathcal{M}(K_i)$'.
da-overclaim.notes: Four substantive structural claims (involution, two-sided inverse, skein-to-mass-formula, fusion closure) are stated as a proved Proposition, but neither the .md nor the Lean supplies a proof of any of them — the Lean (lines 35-48) proves only trivial existentials. The mass-formula identity in item 3 is an additional asserted consequence with no derivation. Conclusion is far stronger than the argument (none) supports.

da-hidden-dof.evidence: hadron-operations-closure.md:19 introduces $Q(q)$ as the skein-coefficient prefactor in the mass formula with no defining expression or canonical-chain origin.
da-hidden-dof.notes: $Q(q)$ appears as a polynomial-in-q weight multiplying $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{Hopf})$ but is never pinned to a specific function of q nor traced to the canonical derivation chain. As written it is an undisclosed degree of freedom in the asserted mass formula. Minor because the block is structural rather than a precision claim, but it should name $Q(q)$ explicitly.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: hadron-operations-closure.md:15-19 — item 3 jumps from 'the q-skein relation resolves any linked composite into a polynomial in q times unlinked constituents' directly to the additive mass formula $\mathcal{M}(\mathfrak{H})=Q(q)\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{Hopf})+\sum_i\mathcal{M}(K_i)$.
da-non-sequitur.notes: The skein resolution acts on knot polynomials / Hecke-algebra elements; the leap to an additive mass decomposition presupposes a homomorphism $\mathcal{M}$ from skein resolutions to MeV masses that is neither stated nor cited. The 'yielding' is a missing-lemma 'therefore'.

da-lean-narrative-divergence.notes: Lean proves $\forall h\,\exists h'\,(h'=\mathrm{op}(h))$ for four opaque axiomatized ops on an `axiom Hadron : ℕ → Type`. The .md claims braiding-is-involution, Hopf-link-has-two-sided-inverse, skein-yields-mass-formula, fusion-is-a-hadron. The Lean is vacuously implied by the existence of total functions and proves none of the .md's content (proof-statement-integrity failure). Additionally `Hadron` and all four operations are `axiom`s, so the theorem is conditional on four un-defined axioms.

da-citation-misuse.evidence: hadron-operations-closure.lean:14,20,46 cite [kock2004] (Kock, Frobenius Algebras and 2D TQFT) for the closure theorem.
da-citation-misuse.notes: Kock 2004 concerns Frobenius algebras / 2D TQFT, not symmetric-product closure under braiding/Hopf-linking/skein/fusion of knot constituents. The citation is at best tangential to the four specific closure claims; no page/section is given. The [manuscript] Ch.4 §10 ref is the only direct backing and is unverifiable here. Minor mis-attribution.

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: hadron-operations-closure.md:12 uses $\mathcal{L}_{Hopf}$ and .md:18 uses $\mathcal{M}(\cdot)$ without definition in-block; 'mass' $\mathcal{M}$ vs hadron mass $\mathfrak{m}$ register.
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: $\mathcal{M}$ (a mass functional), $\mathcal{L}_{Hopf}$ (Hopf-link object), and $Q(q)$ are used without local definitions or `uses[]` links (uses[] lists only def:hadron). Per the notation register physical mass is $\mathfrak{m}$ (fraktur); the calligraphic $\mathcal{M}$ for mass is ambiguous/off-register. Reader cannot resolve the mass formula's terms from this block.

da-physical-implausibility.notes: Read as a hadron mass = sum of constituent masses + a linking term, this is a naive additive (non-binding) decomposition; real hadron/nuclear masses are dominated by binding (mass defect), which an additive '$\sum_i \mathcal{M}(K_i)$ plus a positive linking weight' does not obviously capture without the linking term being negative. Plausibility hinges entirely on the undefined $Q(q)\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{Hopf})$ carrying the binding. Flag, not reject — could be consistent if the linking term is the (negative) binding contribution.

da-referee-verdict.evidence: Rollup of the above: vacuous Lean (lines 35-48), four unproved structural claims stated as a Proposition (.md:6-23), an underived additive mass formula (.md:18-19) with an undefined $Q(q)$.
da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: major-revision. referee_argument: The block is labelled a Proposition but contains no proof of any of its four closure claims; the Lean witness proves only the trivial self-witnessing existential $\exists h'\,(h'=\mathrm{op}(h))$ over four axiomatized operations, which is vacuously true and divergent from the narrative. The asserted mass formula is a non-sequitur from skein resolution with a hidden coefficient $Q(q)$. Either demote to a remark/conjecture or supply real Lean (involution, invertibility, fusion well-definedness) and a derivation of the mass identity.
